speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with postmenopausal bleeding and an adnexal mass. To determine the cause, have you experienced any vaginal bleeding, and if so, how heavy and frequent is it? Additionally, have you noticed any pelvic pain, fever, or changes in your bowel or bladder habits?

speaker: Patient
text: 65-year-old woman. The patient presents with a 2-month history of intermittent postmenopausal bleeding. She denies any recent weight loss, fever, or changes in bladder or bowel habits. No previous history of similar symptoms. She has no history of serious illness and takes no medications regularly.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for those details. Given your age and the findings, I need to assess the characteristics of the adnexal mass. Is the mass on the left or right side, and does it feel solid, cystic, or mixed on examination?

REQUEST TEST: Transvaginal Ultrasound (TVUS)
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pending ultrasound results to differentiate between ovarian neoplasm and benign cyst; high suspicion for ovarian cancer given age and postmenopausal bleeding.
